formTitle: Consolidated General Application Form for Non-Immigrant Visa, Special Work Permit and Provisional Work Permit
checkoutEligibleNote: Not yet decided -- same open business-classification question as the other mapped forms. This mapping covers field-level automation only; checkout eligibility is a separate business decision.
reproductionRightsNote: Confirmed directly on the form itself: 'THIS DOCUMENT MAY BE REPRODUCED AND IS NOT FOR SALE', printed at the top of both pages.
derivedFrom: Measured from 300 DPI rasters of both pages of the real original PDF (downloaded from the private fis-bi-forms-library R2 bucket, originals/BOC04.QF.002.pdf), a Microsoft Word export with a standard (0,0)-origin MediaBox. Same comb-grid template family as BOC04.QF.001: a form-wide uniform cell pitch of 12.96pt, independently re-confirmed on this form via multiple unrelated fields (Present Immigration Status, Character Reference Name, Spouse Name all converged on the same pitch). DD-MMM-YYYY date fields are each three independent comb groups (2/3/4 cells) separated by one blank (unruled) cell-width -- confirmed visually via a pixel-ruled grid-overlay crop of the Expiration of Contract field, which showed three visually distinct bordered box clusters, not one continuous comb. Section IV/V/VI's company and petitioner address/contact fields (House/Unit, Municipality/City, Province+Zip, E-mail Address) are plain bordered boxes with NO internal comb dividers, unlike the applicant's own Section III address fields (which ARE combs) -- confirmed visually and via column darkness scan both finding zero internal dividers. 'Company Name'/'Registration Number' (page 2) share a single uninterrupted 42-cell comb row with no visual divider between them; mapped as two separate charBoxFields split at the cell boundary nearest the 'Registration Number' label's own x-position (confirmed via direct darkness scan: the full row has uniform 12.96pt pitch end to end, no gap).

measurementNotes.uniformCellPitchDiscovery: Re-confirmed the 12.96pt form-wide cell pitch established for BOC04.QF.001 on this sibling form; colsPt generated as evenly-spaced points between measured outer box bounds (cell count = round(width/12.96)).
measurementNotes.dateGroupsAreThreeSeparateCombs: Every DD-MMM-YYYY date field on this form (dateLatestArrival, expiryDate, lastDayAuthStay, dob, child1Dob, child2Dob, expirationContract, aepExpiry, dateOfIssuance, acrExpiry) is three separate comb-box clusters (2 cells/3 cells/4 cells) with one blank, unruled cell-width of empty paper between each cluster -- NOT one continuous 11-cell comb, even though a naive column-darkness scan alone cannot distinguish the two cases (a lone box's own end-border and the next box's own start-border land at the same pitch as an internal divider would). Resolved by direct visual inspection of a pixel-ruled zoom crop of the Expiration of Contract field, which unambiguously shows three separate bordered rectangles.
measurementNotes.companyAddressFieldsAreFreeText: Unlike Section III's applicant address fields (full comb grids), every company/petitioner/character-reference address and e-mail field on page 2 (charRefHouseUnit, charRefMunicipality, charRefProvince, charRefEmail, companyHouseUnit, companyMunicipality, companyProvince, companyEmail) is a plain bordered box with no internal character-cell dividers -- confirmed both by a column darkness scan (zero internal edges found at two different thresholds) and by direct visual crop. Mapped as freeTextFields rather than charBoxFields.
measurementNotes.expiryDateRowCollisionCaught: A first automated pass placed expiryDateDay/Month/Year at the same yTop/yBottom as placeOfIssuance and lastDayAuthStay (y=323.28-335.28), mistakenly treating all three as one row. The first generated test PDF showed placeOfIssuance's and expiryDateYear's text drawing into the exact same cells (an illegible overlaid 'NAIROBI'/'2027'), and the Expiry Date boxes themselves rendered empty. Caught only by the mandatory visual inspection, never by the CLI's successful-generation signal alone. Corrected to the field's own, earlier row (y=298.08-309.84, directly below the 'Expiry Date/Valid Until' label at y=288.8) via fresh pixel measurement -- confirmed by the regenerated PDF showing a clean '14 NOV 2027' in its own row.
measurementNotes.verticalTableDividerContaminatingColumnS: A first automated pass measured charRefLandline, charRefMobile, charRefEmail, and companyEmail's left edges as 307.68pt via a column-darkness scan -- which, for those four fields only, was actually picking up the long vertical rule separating the page's left column (House/Unit/Municipality/Province) from its right column (Contact Numbers/E-mail), not the field's own left border. The first generated test PDF showed each field's first character/glyph rendering one full cell-width to the LEFT of its own box, outside the printed grid entirely. Caught only by the mandatory visual inspection (a CLI 'generate' success with 0 overflow issues gave no indication of this). Corrected by re-scanning each field's columns with the search window's left bound pushed past the divider (x>=310), which recovered each field's true left edge (~319.3-320.1pt, matching the already-correct companyLandline/companyMobile measurements from the same page) -- confirmed by the regenerated PDF showing every character fully inside its own box.
measurementNotes.charRefHouseUnitTwoRows: The Character Reference's 'House/Unit No., Street, Subdivision/Village, Barangay' field is genuinely two stacked plain boxes (not one tall box), confirmed visually -- mapped as charRefHouseUnitLine1/Line2.
measurementNotes.companyNameRegistrationNumberSharedRow: 'Company Name' and 'Registration Number' (page 2, Section IV) share one uninterrupted 42-cell comb box with no visual divider -- confirmed via full-row darkness scan showing uniform 12.96pt pitch end to end. Mapped as two separate charBoxFields (companyName: first 26 cells, registrationNumber: last 16 cells), split at the cell boundary nearest the 'Registration Number' label's own x-position, since each represents a distinct question the customer must answer, consistent with the precedent already established for CGAF-002-Rev3's similarly-shared comb rows.

signatureBlock.note: Wet-ink signatures and date required by the official form -- this form, like its sibling BOC04.QF.001, requires THREE wet-ink elements (Date, Petitioner's Signature, Applicant's Signature). Deliberately left blank -- not populated by this automation. The inline consent-paragraph name blanks ('I, ___, personally or through my agent/representative ___') on page 2 follow the same policy and are not separately mapped.

petitionerSignatureLine.note: Extra, form-specific: this form requires the PETITIONER's own wet-ink signature in addition to the applicant's, distinct from the schema's required signatureLine (the applicant's own). Positioned between the Date and Applicant's Signature columns.

customerPreviewCropBox.note: No separate BI-internal static header/footer region exists on this form -- the Claim Stub (bottom of page 1), the back-page Representative/Accredited Travel Agency claim block (bottom of page 2), and the staff-only Application Number/Received-Reviewed-Approved section are all excluded from customer-audience output structurally (none are mapped as charBoxFields/checkboxFields/freeTextFields at all, or -- for Application Number -- via roles.visibleTo), not via region cropping. The full page is therefore the customer preview region for both pages.

customerVisibleRegions.note: Two regions, the full extent of each of the form's two real PDF pages, same approach as BOC04.QF.001 -- see customerPreviewCropBox note.
